title: Fixed-Point Distribution Converges to Poisson(1) in Total Variation
description: A complete formalization proving that the number of fixed points of a uniformly random permutation of [n] converges in total variation distance to the Poisson(1) distribution: ∑_k |P(X_n = k) - e⁻¹/k!| → 0 as n → ∞. The proof uses the sharp alternating series bound |D(m)/m! - e⁻¹| ≤ 1/(m+1)!, a binomial coefficient identity to sum the pointwise errors, and the factorial decay of 2^(n+1)/(n+1)!.

overview.historicalContext: The Poisson approximation theorem for the number of fixed points of a random permutation is a classical result in probability theory. It follows from the general Poisson approximation for sums of dependent indicator random variables (Chen-Stein method, 1975), but the special case of fixed points has a purely combinatorial proof using the exact derangement formula. The total variation distance is a natural measure of distributional closeness: TV(X_n, Poisson(1)) → 0 means the distributions become indistinguishable in the strongest sense.
overview.problemStatement:
Let X_n = #{i : σ(i) = i} for a uniformly random permutation σ of [n] = {1,...,n}.

Let Z ~ Poisson(1) with P(Z = k) = e⁻¹/k!.

**Main Theorem**: The total variation distance converges to 0:
  TV(X_n, Z) = (1/2) · ∑_k |P(X_n = k) - e⁻¹/k!| → 0 as n → ∞.

**Key formula**: P(X_n = k) = D(n-k) / ((n-k)! · k!) for k ≤ n, and 0 for k > n.

**Quantitative bound**: ∑_k |P(X_n = k) - e⁻¹/k!| ≤ 2^(n+1)/(n+1)! + ∑_{k>n} e⁻¹/k!
overview.proofStrategy:
**Step 1 (PMF formula)**: P(X_n = k) = D(n-k)/((n-k)!·k!) comes from choosing which k positions are fixed and counting derangements of the rest.

**Step 2 (Pointwise bound)**: For k ≤ n, |P(X_n=k) - e⁻¹/k!| = |D(n-k)/(n-k)! - e⁻¹| / k! ≤ 1/((n-k+1)!·k!) using the sharp bound from derangements-convergence.

**Step 3 (Binomial identity)**: ∑_{k=0}^n 1/((n+1-k)!·k!) = ∑_{k=0}^n C(n+1,k)/(n+1)! ≤ 2^(n+1)/(n+1)! using ∑_{k=0}^n C(n+1,k) ≤ 2^(n+1).

**Step 4 (Tail bound)**: ∑_{k>n} e⁻¹/k! is the tail of a convergent series, tending to 0.

**Step 5 (Squeeze)**: The total variation sum is bounded by the sum of Steps 3 and 4, both tending to 0.
keyInsights: The exact formula P(X_n = k) = D(n-k)/((n-k)!·k!) reduces total variation convergence to the pointwise convergence of D(m)/m! to e⁻¹, a purely analytic question.
The binomial coefficient identity ∑_{k=0}^n C(n+1,k)/(n+1)! ≤ 2^(n+1)/(n+1)! beautifully packages the sum of pointwise errors into a single factorial-decay bound.
The proof avoids the Chen-Stein method entirely, relying instead on the classical alternating series bound from the derangement formula — a purely combinatorial approach to a probabilistic theorem.
Summability of the Poisson(1) PMF is equivalent to the convergence of ∑ e⁻¹/k! = e⁻¹ · e = 1, a normalization that is itself a consequence of the exponential series.
prerequisites: Derangements and the convergence D(n)/n! → 1/e (see derangements-convergence)
Total variation distance for probability distributions
The Poisson distribution and its PMF

conclusion.summary: Total variation convergence of the fixed-point distribution to Poisson(1) is fully formalized with an explicit upper bound 2^(n+1)/(n+1)! + tail, all machine-verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. The proof is a clean analytical argument combining the alternating series bound for derangements with the binomial theorem.
conclusion.implications: This result is a formal statement of the classical 'hat-check problem' convergence: the probability distribution of the number of correctly-returned hats in a random permutation converges (in the strongest measure) to the Poisson(1) distribution. It is a canonical example of the Poisson approximation phenomenon that appears throughout probability theory.
openQuestions: Can the quantitative bound TV(X_n, Poisson(1)) ≤ 1/n be established formally? This follows from the Chen-Stein method and is sharper than the 2^(n+1)/(n+1)! bound here.
Can the total variation convergence be extended to the joint distribution of fixed points of powers of the permutation?

sections.title: Section I: Alternating Series Bound for Derangements
sections.summary: Builds the alternating series machinery from the ground up. Defines altTerm k = (-1)^k/k! and altPartialSum n. Proves summability via summable_pow_div_factorial. Establishes exp_neg_one_eq_tsum (e⁻¹ = ∑ altTerm k) and the reusable tsum_split lemma. Key inequalities: alt_nonneg and alt_le_first (proved by pairwise strong induction), then alt_tail_bound and derangement_rate (|D(m)/m! - e⁻¹| ≤ 1/(m+1)!).

sections.title: Section II: Fixed-Point PMF and Poisson(1) PMF
sections.summary: Defines fixedPtPMF n k = D(n-k)/((n-k)!·k!) for k ≤ n, else 0; and poisson1PMF k = e⁻¹/k!. Proves nonnegativity, zero-outside-support, and summability for both. summable_fixedPtPMF uses summable_of_ne_finset_zero; summable_poisson1 uses summable_pow_div_factorial 1.

sections.title: Section III: Pointwise Error Bound
sections.summary: pointwise_bound: for k ≤ n, |P(X_n=k) - e⁻¹/k!| ≤ 1/((n-k+1)!·k!). Proved by fixedPtPMF_sub (algebraic rearrangement) combined with derangement_rate(n-k) and div_le_div_of_nonneg_right.

sections.title: Section IV: Finite Sum Bound via Binomial Identity
sections.summary: inv_fact_eq_choose: rewrites 1/((n+1-k)!·k!) = C(n+1,k)/(n+1)! using Nat.choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial. finite_sum_bound: ∑_{k=0}^n 1/((n+1-k)!·k!) ≤ 2^(n+1)/(n+1)! by summing the binomial identity and bounding ∑_{k=0}^n C(n+1,k) ≤ 2^(n+1) (dropping the k=n+1 term from (1+1)^(n+1)).

sections.title: Section V: Poisson(1) Tail Convergence
sections.summary: poisson1_tail_tendsto: the tail ∑_{k>n} e⁻¹/k! → 0 as n → ∞. Proved by rewriting the tail using tsum_split, then showing the difference (total sum) - (partial sum) converges to 0 via summable_poisson1.hasSum.tendsto_sum_nat composed with tendsto_add_atTop_nat 1.

sections.title: Section VI: Summability of TV Integrand
sections.summary: summable_tv_integrand n: proves ∑ |fixedPtPMF n k - poisson1PMF k| is summable. Uses Summable.of_nonneg_of_le: bounded above by (fixedPtPMF n k) + (poisson1PMF k), which is summable since both components are.

sections.title: Section VII: Main Theorem — Total Variation Convergence
sections.summary: tvSum n = ∑' k, |fixedPtPMF n k - poisson1PMF k| (the ℓ¹ distance, = 2 × TV). tvSum_le: the key upper bound 2^(n+1)/(n+1)! + tail via tsum_split + finite_sum_bound. fixedPt_tv_tendsto: main theorem, squeeze_zero with pow_div_fact_tendsto and poisson1_tail_tendsto. Bonus: derangement_prob_tendsto recovers D(n)/n! → e⁻¹ via squeeze_zero_norm.

crossReferences.description: The sharp bound |D(n)/n! - e⁻¹| ≤ 1/(n+1)! is the key analytic input to the pointwise error estimate in the TV convergence proof.
Both entries develop probabilistic approximation arguments; the fixed-point distribution is a canonical example of Poisson approximation via the second moment method.
Both proofs rely heavily on Mathlib's summability infrastructure (tsum, Summable, summable_pow_div_factorial).
